title: Rav Hamnuna the Scribe
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 6:2: he asked Rabbi Chaninah, who did not answer him, and then asked Rabbi Yirmeyah. Hyman distinguishes him from the Rav Hamnuna the Scribe in Kohelet Rabbah 7:7, whom he takes to be the first Rav Hamnuna, the teacher of Rabbi Chanina bar Chama. The supplied text places that figure in Rava’s days.

notes.text: The speaker is Rava in the supplied passage. Hyman’s identification with the first Rav Hamnuna and the associated teacher/generation claim remain conjectural and chronologically problematic. The notice stays held; no automatic Rav-to-Rabbi emendation resolves it.

The supplied phrase is בימי רבא, “in Rava’s days,” rather than Rabbah’s. Rava is named in the chronological description, not as the speaker in the preceding question. Hyman’s distinction of two figures called Hamnuna and the first figure’s relationship as teacher of Rabbi Chanina bar Chama remain attributed claims whose chronology requires investigation. A proposed רבא/רבי emendation is only a possibility; no source letters or identities are silently changed.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. I, p. 379) reads בימי רבי, “in Rabbi’s days.” The supplied Hebrew reads בימי רבא, “in Rava’s days.” In the consulted Kohelet Rabbah 7:7, Chanina says he read before Rabbi Hamnuna the Scribe of Babylonia, in the account of Rabbi Judah HaNasi’s appointments. Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 6:2 names Rav Hamnuna the Scribe in the exchange with Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Yirmeyah. The distinction between the two figures and the teacher relationship as stated here remain Hyman’s interpretation.
